Compute WAIC for model comparison

Source: R/waic.R
waic.Rd

Computes the Widely Applicable Information Criterion (WAIC) for a fitted phase model. This provides an estimate of out-of-sample predictive accuracy.

Usage

waic(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A phase_fit object

...

Additional arguments (unused)

Value

A list with components:

  • waic: The WAIC value (lower is better)

  • lppd: Log pointwise predictive density

  • p_waic: Effective number of parameters

  • se: Standard error of WAIC

Details

WAIC is computed as: $$WAIC = -2 * (lppd - p_{WAIC})$$

where lppd is the log pointwise predictive density and p_WAIC is the effective number of parameters (variance of the log-likelihood).

For phase models, the log-likelihood of each observation is that given the earlier observations of its unit, marginalised over the latent phases, at every posterior draw.

References

Watanabe, S. (2010). Asymptotic equivalence of Bayes cross validation and widely applicable information criterion in singular learning theory. Journal of Machine Learning Research 11, 3571-3594.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
fit1 <- fit_phaseR(model1, data)
fit2 <- fit_phaseR(model2, data)
waic(fit1)$waic
waic(fit2)$waic
} # }
